basis: HSV-1 labialis characteristically affects the external lip vermilion and adjacent skin; intraoral mucosal infection is not required.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: herpes labialis does not require oral mucosal involvement; characteristic lesions affect external lip vermilion.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: infectious vesicles and ulcers of the lip vermilion and adjacent skin define herpes labialis.

basis: Joint anomalies define syndrome; ptosis 80-99%, intellectual disability and coagulation abnormalities each 30-79%. Evidence derives from two patients.

decisions.ocular: involved: eyelid ptosis occurs in 80-99%; it accompanies the defining skeletal syndrome rather than constituting a separate defining eye disorder.

basis: Sensory-autonomic neuropathy and spastic paraplegia define disease; skin ulcers occur in 80-99%. Muscle wasting is neurogenic; osteomyelitis occurs in 25%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy in 4/4 reflects denervation from neuropathy, without evidence of direct skeletal-muscle disease.

basis: Ehrlichia directly infects monocytes/macrophages; acute hepatic inflammation and hepatocellular injury occur in approximately 70-90%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic inflammation with hepatocellular injury and aminotransferase elevation occurs in approximately 70-90% during infection.

basis: Defined by deep dermal/subcutaneous edema. The umbrella does not establish an immune mechanism; episodic mucosal swelling does not establish additional lasting organ damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: angioedema alone does not establish immune-mediated disease; this umbrella includes nonimmune bradykinin-mediated and drug-induced forms.

basis: Lung is the defining target of this hereditary neoplastic susceptibility. The primary label identifies its organ specificity without asserting existing cancer or lung injury.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary neoplasia defines the susceptibility syndrome; the exclusion of later risks prevents additional involved organs.

basis: Patellar defects; neutropenia 5/6 with infections 5/7. Neurologic: microcephaly 6/6 and intellectual disability 2/2. Microtia 8/8 omitted at cap; hearing impairment unreported.

decisions.haematologic: primary: neutropenia in 5/6 establishes a common blood-cell disorder; the mechanism-axis rule places this in primary.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 2/2 assessed, supported by microcephaly in 6/6, establishes common neurodevelopmental involvement.
decisions.otologic: none at cap: microtia occurs in 8/8, but hearing impairment is unreported; prioritize skeletal, blood, immune and neurodevelopmental dysfunction.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome; ear canal/stapes defects, cleft palate and VSD each reported in 1/1 assessed. Scoliosis 1/1 omitted at cap; population frequencies uncertain.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: VSD in 1/1 assessed supports structural cardiac involvement; rare coarctation and ventricular hypoplasia are not relied upon.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: scoliosis in 1/1 qualifies, but structural cardiac, ear and palatal defects receive priority; population frequency remains uncertain.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal atresia and absent stapes each occur in 1/1 assessed; structural ear dysfunction accompanies the neurodevelopmental syndrome.

basis: Inherited chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis is defined by Candida infection of skin, nails and oral mucosa. Endocrine findings lack adequate frequency evidence.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: chronic oral mucosal Candida infection is part of the defining mucocutaneous disease; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Bacterial presence in urine defines a urinary-system finding; asymptomatic colonization does not by itself establish urinary infection or tissue injury.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: bacteriuria can represent asymptomatic colonization; bacterial presence alone does not establish an infectious disease.
